paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption: Inter-annotator agreement compared to sample-level ambiguity standard deviation and sample-level maximum ambiguity values.
model_annotation: The figure presents two side-by-side vertical bar charts illustrating inter-annotator agreement (Fleiss’ Kappa) in relation to two ambiguity measures: sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (left panel) and sample-level maximum ambiguity (right panel). In both panels, the horizontal axis contains the ambiguity categories and the vertical axis represents agreement values; the vertical axis is labeled “Fleiss Kappa,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately 0.0 to 0.9 with regularly spaced tick labels at about 0.2 intervals (0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8). In the left panel, the horizontal axis is labeled “Ambiguity Std” and shows four category tick labels in increasing numeric order: 0.0, 0.47, 0.82, and 0.94; the corresponding bars are shaded from darker teal to lighter blue and have value annotations above them: 0.0 has a bar at about 0.88, 0.47 has a bar at about 0.46, 0.82 has a very short bar at about 0.03, and 0.94 has a bar at about 0.24. In the right panel, the horizontal axis is labeled “Max Ambiguity” and shows three categories in increasing order: 1, 2, and 3; the bars use a similar dark-to-light teal/blue palette and are annotated with values of about 0.89 for category 1, about 0.46 for category 2, and about 0.23 for category 3. No legend is shown, the bars are not stacked or grouped beyond their single-series arrangement, and the primary visual emphasis comes from the numeric value labels placed above each bar.
